destination.name: Coffin Bay
destination.tagline: An oyster-farming village on a calm bay, beside a wild coastal national park.
destination.description: Coffin Bay is a small village on the western side of the Eyre Peninsula, about 40 minutes' drive from Port Lincoln. Matthew Flinders named the bay after his friend Sir Isaac Coffin, and the town is known for its oysters. Coffin Bay National Park to the west has windswept cliffs, dunes, surf beaches and sheltered bays, and Kellidie Bay Conservation Park lies to the east. An 8 km foreshore trail follows the shore past the jetty and the oyster-growing waters.
whyVisit: Taste oysters fresh from the bay
Explore a wild coastal national park

goodToKnow.title: Know your 4WD access
goodToKnow.detail: The park's northern beaches need a high-clearance 4WD, while Yangie Bay and Point Avoid can be reached in a 2WD.

goodToKnow.title: Pay park entry first
goodToKnow.detail: Vehicle entry to Coffin Bay National Park is $14.40 and must be paid before you go in.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the warm months for swimming, boating and fishing on the bay, and the village is busiest then.
